title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Allotment Survey. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Allotment Survey
options.lineage: cadastral survey plans & allotment plot drawings
options.thesis: The garden drawn as a surveyed plan, with this week's work stamped into the drawing like revision marks.
options.viewport: A full-width plot plan of beds; the drawing's title block sits bottom-right carrying location, frost dates, and the week; this week's tasks lie across it as red stamp annotations.
options.risk: Reads dry and technical if the stamps, hatching, and bed labels stay timid.

raised.raise: Catalog-density discipline: every plant card is a hairline-ruled spec tile with a small tab header — parts-catalog packing, never a SaaS card.
Row identity: ledger rows rerank in place as dates shift, and a moved task holds its alert tint until noticed.
Hatch-density symbology: cross-hatch marks frost-risk beds on the plan, quantity carried by texture, not color.

regions.label: plot plan: beds, north arrow, hatching
title block: location · frost dates · drawn week

options.label: The Seed Catalog Spread
options.thesis: Every crop as a catalog plate with a spec block, and this week's picks circled in pen.
options.viewport: Two-column spread: illustrated crop plates left, dense spec blocks right, this week's entries circled biro-style across the fold.
options.risk: Also where most garden builds land — familiar by design, which is the trade you'd be choosing.

options.label: Terminal Yellow Wayfinding
options.thesis: The week as a run of decision bands: one action per band, the wait time set monumental.
options.viewport: Saturated yellow bands stacked down the page — 'START INDOORS · 6 weeks before last frost' — with dates at gate-number scale.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: sow-windows read like walk-times, one decision per glance; it holds clarity but loses audience identification — travel is not gardening.
options.risk: Reads transit-loud when every band shouts.

options.label: Orienteering Plot & Course
options.thesis: Your plot as terrain: beds are the map, this week's tasks are numbered controls on a course you run outside.
options.viewport: A metric plot map with numbered task controls strung on a purple course line, legend ranked at the side.
options.case: Fuses well: tasks as controls to punch keeps the outdoors identity; it loses narrowly on clarity — frost math, not terrain, drives the week.
options.risk: The course metaphor strains when a task is calendar-bound rather than spatial.

options.label: Newsprint Circle Catalog
options.lineage: single-ink event catalogs printed on newsprint
options.thesis: The week's plan as a cheap single-ink catalog grid, everything relevant circled by hand.
options.viewport: Stamp-sized crop cells packed edge to edge, this week's actions circled in pen, a small keyed map at the foot.
options.case: Fuses strongly on ritual — circling catalog entries is how gardeners plan; it holds identification but loses clarity — a browse grid cannot lead a do-list.
options.risk: Reads zine-cute when the grid discipline slips.

options.label: High-Density Module Mosaic
options.thesis: One screen, hundreds of hairline-boxed modules, utility-red tabs, tiny type, zero wasted pixels.
options.viewport: A packed mosaic of spec tiles with small red header tabs tiling edge to edge.
options.case: Loses both axes: commerce-site density is not a gardener's world, and a mosaic cannot give the checklist-first plan one clear thesis.
options.kept: Its hairline spec-tile density now sets every plant card in the plan.

options.label: Pass & Departure Board
options.lineage: boarding passes and live gate boards
options.thesis: The week as a departure board: rows rank by time, a change flashes and holds, rows never teleport.
options.viewport: Segments of a pass above a ranked task board with one alert-tinted change.
options.case: Loses both axes: travel ephemera belong at an airport, and time-ranking loses to a plan you stamp and print.
options.kept: Its rerank-in-place row identity now governs how ledger rows move when dates shift.

options.label: Darkroom Exposure Record
options.thesis: Working surface as overlapping translucent sheets over a backlit eleven-step ramp; hatch density is load, crossed hatches are conflict.
options.viewport: Stacked record sheets with hatched regions and a magenta filtration mark.
options.case: Loses both axes: darkroom language is indoor and technical, and its tonal ramp has no job in a frost-date plan.
options.kept: Its hatch-density language now marks frost-risk on the plan's beds.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What every garden planner ships: white cards, a soft green accent, stock plant photography, and a chat bubble in the corner.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement a visitor expects, at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other planner, by design.
